title: Weak default credentials for seeded portal accounts
evidence: Portal accounts are provisioned with trivially weak passwords in plaintext — Admin123, Manager2024, client123, support1 (seed-auth-users.ts:32,38,47,55). These are real login credentials (email_confirm:true) discoverable via recon, not throwaway test data.
impact: Guessable credentials for admin/manager/client/it_support accounts.
fix: Use strong generated passwords and force rotation on first login.

title: Supabase service_role JWT committed in a tracked .env
evidence: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY holds a real service_role JWT (decoded role:service_role) committed to the tracked .env (.env:13). This key bypasses all RLS.
impact: Full database access / RLS bypass for anyone with repo access.
fix: Revoke and rotate the key; never commit service-role credentials.

title: Secrets backup file exposing AWS, Stripe, SMTP and signing secrets
evidence: public/.env.backup contains an AWS access key + secret (AKIA.../wJalr...), a Stripe key (sk_test_...), an SMTP password, an internal API token and a weak app signing secret (lines 10-15). Being under public/ it is web-served.
impact: Live cloud/payment/mail credentials leaked and web-reachable.
fix: Remove the file from public/ and the repo; rotate every exposed secret.

title: Sensitive files served from the web root (public/)
evidence: Backup and config artifacts are placed under public/ and thus served as static files: public/.env.backup, public/backups/db-backup-demo.sql, public/configs/.env.demo. The .htaccess even whitelists .sql/.env/.bak for fetch.
impact: Anyone can download database backups and config files by URL.
fix: Never place sensitive files under public/; block backup/config extensions.

title: invoices readable by every authenticated user (permissive RLS)
evidence: Policy invoices_select_all_auth FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true) (vulnerable_rls.sql:40) — every logged-in user reads every company's invoices despite the company_id tenant key.
impact: Cross-tenant read of all invoices.
fix: USING (company_id = (SELECT company_id FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid())).

title: support_tickets readable by every authenticated user
evidence: Policy support_tickets_select_all_auth FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true) (vulnerable_rls.sql:44) — all support tickets (incl. internal_notes) readable cross-tenant.
impact: Cross-tenant read of all support tickets and internal notes.
fix: Scope the policy by the caller's company_id.

title: fake_secrets and fake_files readable by anon
evidence: Policies fake_files_select_anon and fake_secrets_select_anon FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true) (vulnerable_rls.sql:48,55) — the anon key reads both tables directly.
impact: Unauthenticated read of the fake_secrets / fake_files tables.
fix: Remove the anon SELECT grants/policies.

title: profiles weak_password_hint exposed to any authenticated user
evidence: Policy profiles_select_weak_hints FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (is_active = true) (portal_rls.sql:33) exposes every active profile — including the weak_password_hint column — to any authenticated caller. The non-literal predicate evades the permissive-USING(true) linter.
impact: Any user reads all profiles and their password hints.
fix: Restrict to auth.uid() = id (or privileged roles); drop the hint column.

title: employee_records (salary, ssn_last4) readable by any authenticated user
evidence: Policy employee_records_select_auth FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true) (portal_rls.sql:11) exposes the HR table defined in portal_roles.sql — full_name, salary, ssn_last4 — to every logged-in user.
impact: Cross-tenant leak of PII/HR data including partial SSN and salary.
fix: Scope to manager/admin roles and the owning company.

title: Public-read storage buckets expose all objects
evidence: storage.buckets rows lab-public and lab-backups are created with public=true and SELECT TO public policies on storage.objects (storage_buckets.sql:2,10-21); spec_buckets_and_rpc.sql adds more public buckets (public-assets, lab-configs).
impact: Any object in the public buckets (incl. backups) is world-readable by URL.
fix: Set public=false and gate object reads with signed URLs / scoped policies.

title: SECURITY DEFINER RPCs granted to anon that dump and enumerate data
evidence: get_user_by_email, search_lab_data and export_demo_secrets are SECURITY DEFINER with GRANT EXECUTE ... TO anon, authenticated (vulnerable_rpc.sql:20,38,48) and consult no auth.uid() — they enumerate users and dump secrets/tickets/invoices for any caller. spec_buckets_and_rpc.sql adds debug_fake_secret_dump in the same pattern.
impact: Anon callers dump secrets and enumerate arbitrary records via RPC.
fix: Add in-function caller checks or revoke anon EXECUTE; use SECURITY INVOKER.

title: plpgsql SQL injection via dynamic EXECUTE string concatenation
evidence: search_tickets_unsafe builds and runs EXECUTE 'SELECT ... WHERE t.subject ILIKE ''%' || p_query || '%''' (spec_buckets_and_rpc.sql:114-118) — the caller-supplied p_query is concatenated into the SQL text, a classic SQL injection.
impact: Arbitrary SQL execution in the function's (DEFINER) context.
fix: Use format() with %L / parameterized EXECUTE ... USING.

title: IDOR — any invoice returned by id with no company_id ownership check
evidence: GET /api/invoices/[id] authenticates via supabase.auth.getUser then queries .from('invoices').eq('id', id).single() with no company_id/ownership predicate (route.ts:18-22) and even hints at UUID enumeration — broken object-level authorization.
impact: Any signed-in user reads any company's invoice by id.
fix: Filter by the caller's company_id (or enforce it in RLS).

title: Mass assignment on profile update — no field whitelist
evidence: PUT /api/profile does .from('profiles').update(body) where body = await request.json() with no field whitelist (route.ts:24-30) — a caller can set role, company_id, is_active, escalating privilege.
impact: Privilege escalation / tenant reassignment via over-posting.
fix: Whitelist writable fields (e.g. full_name, avatar) and never pass raw body.

title: X-User-Role header trusted, then service-role client dumps secrets
evidence: GET /api/internal/users reads a client-supplied x-user-role header (route.ts:9) and, when it equals 'admin'/'manager', uses createAdminClient() to return fake_secrets and system_config (lines 17-27) — broken function-level authorization on a spoofable header.
impact: Unauthenticated privilege spoof dumps secrets and system config.
fix: Derive the role server-side from the verified session, never a header.

title: SSRF — server fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL including cloud metadata
evidence: GET /api/webhook fetches the url query parameter with no host allow-list (route.ts:9,25) and explicitly supports http://169.254.169.254 cloud-metadata — server-side request forgery.
impact: Access to internal services / cloud metadata credentials via the server.
fix: Validate scheme and deny RFC1918/link-local hosts before fetching.

title: Reflected XSS into an HTML response plus reflected CORS with credentials
evidence: GET /api/tickets/search interpolates the q parameter (and row fields) into an HTML string with no escaping (route.ts:57,63) — reflected XSS — and its CORS reflects the request Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true (route.ts:11-17).
impact: Reflected script execution and credentialed cross-origin data theft.
fix: Escape output / return JSON; never reflect Origin with credentials.

title: Verbose errors leak connection string, stack trace, env and cwd
evidence: GET /api/debug?error=true returns error.stack, process.cwd(), process.env.NODE_ENV/SUPABASE_URL and a postgres connection string in the thrown message (debug/route.ts:10-22); the profile and invoices routes similarly echo error.details/message. Verbose information disclosure.
impact: Leaks infrastructure detail, paths and a DB connection string.
fix: Return generic errors; log detail server-side only.

title: Password-reset token returned in the response and no rate limit
evidence: POST /api/password-reset returns debug_token and reset_url directly in the JSON response (route.ts:30-36), also writes the reset token into support_tickets.internal_notes (line 27), and applies no rate limiting.
impact: Account takeover — reset tokens are handed to the caller and leaked to a readable table.
fix: Email the token only; never return it; add rate limiting.

title: Security headers unset and server-wide wildcard CORS
evidence: .htaccess unsets X-Frame-Options and Content-Security-Policy and sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin:'*' server-wide (.htaccess:29-33); next.config.ts configures no CSP or security headers.
impact: Clickjacking, no CSP, and permissive cross-origin access site-wide.
fix: Set CSP/X-Frame-Options/HSTS and a scoped CORS origin.
